reasons: The MFN in § 7.2 runs the wrong way — it obliges Customer (Redwood) to give Vendor terms no less favourable than those offered to any other technology supplier — squarely within the rule's detection guidance for a burdening MFN, and open-ended (no product scope, no term, no comparison carve-outs), i.e. the walk-away position.

The redline deletes § 7.2 in full, which matches the redline guidance ('delete the obligation on Customer') and is the minimal edit reaching the preferred position; no Vendor-granted MFN exists in the document, so nothing beneficial to Customer is removed.

The comment is accurate, concise, first-person plural, correctly prefixed, states what changed and why, notes the conflict with § 12.3 (Vendor's acknowledgment of no most-favoured-customer commitment), and preserves the point that MFN in our favour remains welcome.
Deterministic check confirms the operation applies; the high changed-character ratio is inherent to a justified full-clause deletion.
